earlier_scan.note: Meakambut is essentially undocumented (only Kassell et al. 2017 survey / Haberland 1966 noted); no phonological description exists to reach

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison, Bonnie MacKenzie & Margaret Potter. 2017. Three Arafundi Languages: A Sociolinguistic Profile of Andai, Nanubae, and Tapei. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2017-003. Dallas: SIL International. 60 pp.
sources.note: Meakambut/Mongolo not surveyed: p.2 fn.5 'no linguistic data was collected from the Mongolo people'. The report's only stress remark (sec. 2.3.2.2, p.17) is for the Wambrumas (Nanubae, nanu1240) wordlist: 'Stress was only marked on Wambrumas list... It appears that stress was generally on the ultimate syllable. If there is a suffix or it is a compound word, the last syllable of the stem is stressed and there may be secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme.' Nothing on Meakambut.

'Meakambut ways of speaking: audio-visual documentation of communication practices in a small semi-nomadic hunter-and-gatherer society in Papua New Guinea' and 'Traditional ecological knowledge of the Awiakay and Meakambut, Papua New Guinea' (eldp.net project list; deposits at ELAR)

sources.citation: Heeschen, Volker & Darja Hoenigman. 2026. Songs in Eipo, Yale, Awiakay and Meakambut, four Papuan languages. In Riesberg, Reinöhl & Hellwig (eds.), The Documentarist Turn (SLCS 240), 314-342. Amsterdam: John Benjamins. OA, CC BY-NC-ND. doi:10.1075/slcs.240.13hee
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.2 p.317: Meakambut is an Arafundi-family language with 64 semi-nomadic speakers south of Awiakay land; Hoenigman has visited them since 2015. Chapter concerns song language; Meakambut do not compose songs in their own language. No phonology or prosody of speech.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: Arafundi River (DokuWiki page, UZH host, last modified 2024) and Andai subpage.
sources.note: Secondary comparative site. Reports Mongolo = Meakambut with no data collected (after Kassell 2005), Hoenigman 2015:46 allies Meakambut with Andai, and an undated SIL 'Penari' vocabulary may represent Meakambut speech. Historical phonology gives proto-Arafundi segments only; no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Hoenigman, Darja. 2015. 'The talk goes many ways': registers of language and modes of performance in Kanjimei, East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. doi:10.25911/5c4834f04778a
sources.note: Thesis is on Awiakay (awia1234). p.46: author recorded basic wordlists among 'the nomadic Meakambut' (details in Hoenigman 2007 MA pp.135-144, 261-272); Fig. 1.4 puts Meakambut under 'Upper Arafundi' with Anday etc. Appendix A (Awiakay grammar notes) has phoneme charts and only says each diphthong 'carries a single stress' while vowel sequences carry separate stresses ([wa-i] first syllable primary, second secondary); no word-stress placement rule, and nothing on Meakambut phonology.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. (entry 138 Meakambut, p.40)
sources.note: Nothing; village list (Avieme, Isangan?, Pundugum, Tungum, uncensused villages at head of Arafundi River) and a comment that Meakambut is closely related to Alfendio but his data suggest a language boundary.
